title: Test-Time Accuracy-Cost Control in Neural Simulators via Recurrent-Depth
claim: A modular encoder, iterated core block and decoder let users dial test-time compute by choosing the number of recurrent iterations.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, 3D volumes top corners, control-knob inset above
description: A single-row block diagram flows left to right. A 3D volumetric turbulence cube (dark purple with orange and yellow streaks) sits at top left as the input. A black arrow points down to a tan rounded box labeled 'encoder'. An orange arrow leads to a small stacked bar of three colored slabs, labeled c (tan), z0 (pink), and zk (teal). A teal arrow then leads to a large teal box labeled 'recurrent-depth block'. A teal loop line labeled '×K' runs back above the block and feeds into a tan 'decoder' box on the right. A black arrow points up from the decoder to a similar output cube at top right. At top center, a dashed teal inset reads 'set recurrent steps K' and shows a dial running from 'low' to 'high'. The dial inset draws the eye first, then the left-to-right flow. Tan marks the encoder and decoder, and teal marks the recurrent part.
caption: Schematic of the Recurrent-Depth Simulator (RecurrSim) framework. RecurrSim consists of three main components: an encoder, a recurrent-depth block, and a decoder. At test-time, the user is able to control the accuracy-cost trade-off by setting the number of recurrent iterations K.
abstract: Accuracy-cost trade-offs are a fundamental aspect of scientific computing. Classical numerical methods inherently offer such a trade-off: increasing resolution, order, or precision typically yields more accurate solutions at higher computational cost. We introduce \textbf{Recurrent-Depth Simulator} (\textbf{RecurrSim}) an architecture-agnostic framework that enables explicit test-time control over accuracy-cost trade-offs in neural simulators without requiring retraining or architectural redesign. By setting the number of recurrent iterations $K$, users can generate fast, less-accurate simulations for exploratory runs or real-time control loops, or increase $K$ for more-accurate simulations in critical applications or offline studies. We demonstrate RecurrSim's effectiveness across fluid dynamics benchmarks (Burgers, Korteweg-De Vries, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky), achieving physically faithful simulations over long horizons even in low-compute settings. On high-dimensional 3D compressible Navier-Stokes simulations with 262k points, a 0.8B parameter RecurrFNO outperforms 1.6B parameter baselines while using 13.5\% less training memory. RecurrSim consistently delivers superior accuracy-cost trade-offs compared to alternative adaptive-compute models, including Deep Equilibrium and diffusion-based approaches. We further validate broad architectural compatibility: RecurrViT reduces error accumulation by 90\% compared to standard Vision Transformers on Active Matter, while RecurrUPT matches UPT performance on ShapeNet-Car using 44\% fewer parameters.
